projects.label: 28 October 2026 · Winner
projects.title: Data for Good Challenge
projects.description: Won Emergent Leuven’s Data for Good Challenge with a team-built prototype for Artsen Zonder Grenzen (Médecins Sans Frontières, MSF). We combined retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) with a knowledge graph to help staff and volunteers find relevant reports, protocols, and lessons from past crises faster, designed for local use without internet access.

projectDirectory.label: Interactive data project
projectDirectory.title: RoadLens — Belgian Road Safety
projectDirectory.description: An interactive exploration of Belgian injury crashes from 2017 to 2024. Explore locations, road types, severity, vehicles and weather, with data quality limitations explained alongside the charts.

projectDirectory.label: Featured project
projectDirectory.title: Regulatory Watch
projectDirectory.description: For a multinational bank, I worked on automating the monitoring of regulatory developments. The challenge was keeping track of changes over time so the team could review new information.

projectDirectory.label: 28 October 2026 · Winner
projectDirectory.title: Data for Good Challenge
projectDirectory.description: Our team built an offline search prototype for Médecins Sans Frontières at Emergent Leuven’s Data for Good Challenge. We cleaned and indexed MSF documents before deployment so volunteers could search reports and protocols on a local server without an internet connection. A knowledge graph linked related documents by topic and country, helping users follow a search result back to its sources.

projectDirectory.label: Animal health research
projectDirectory.title: Goat Activity & Health Monitoring
projectDirectory.description: I explored how unsupervised learning could identify patterns in goats’ activity from sensor readings without requiring every behaviour to be labelled by hand. The research question was whether changes in those patterns could flag a goat for a closer health check.
